hypothesis: With identical native axial-history softening, the direction of applied displacement relative to a precrack changes notch localization, cohesive/adhesive competition and retained internal connectivity. This tests geometry/loading effects before introducing mixed-mode failure.
only_changed_factor: top prescribed displacement direction z versus x

geometry.notch: reference z=0 segment intersections with x<=-50 um; initial geometry only
geometry.m: immutable full original star before precut

loading.waveform: half cosine; same 240 um net separation used by the prior +/-120 um small specimen
loading.release: At 2 ms remove displacement constraint on top and integrate its existing x,v. No material bond is cut at release. Grip-connected components before release are not free fragments.

integration.method: Exact VV coordinate forecast with typed damage; halve BEFORE native commit, verify forecast against accepted x/d. No rejected native state is reused.

limitations: Finite 3D specimen, thickness=2.66 delta, ligament=2.66 delta. Not continuum-converged, not calibrated Gc, not a real V3 rerun. Only two pre-frozen directions; no amplitude or parameter search.
expected_cost: Two ~10000-step cases, measured wall/RSS retained; no arbitrary RSS or wall-clock stop.
